newsitem.title: JAPAN: Comson to settle promissory notes after Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Comson to settle promissory notes after Wednesday.

text.p: Machinery maker Comson Corp said on Friday that it would settle after Wednesday of next week promissory notes worth 80 million yen that were due today.
The settlement will be made using funds from a convertible bond issue, the company said.

"We confirmed that the payment of the CB (convertible bond) will be on August 19. We will settle the promissory notes and repay debts (using funds from the CB issue)," Comson president Toshimi Matsuda told a news conference.
On August 1, Comson said that it had postponed the settlement of promissory notes worth 80 million yen until August 15.
The company said on August 6 that it would issue $10 million worth of dollar-denominated convertible bonds on August 19 and $10 million worth of dollar-denominated warrants on September 17.
Matsuda said that six Hong Kong-based investment companies would buy CBs. He did not offer further details.

He said that Comson had promissory notes worth 50 million yen due on Wednesday of next week. The company also has promissory notes and debts due on August 31, he said, although he did not disclose the amount.
Matsuda said that Comson, which in July revised its earnings forecast for the year to November 30, 1997, wanted to revise its earnings outlook again by the end of this month.
"I would like to announce more precise figures," he said.

In July, Comson said that it would post a parent current loss of 1.79 billion yen in 1996/97, against its previous forecast of a current profit of 398 million yen. The company recorded a parent current profit in 1995/96 of 80 million yen.
